title: The same breakout rules made 92% on NQ, 30% on ES and lost 48% on gold
author: person-person12
selftext:
I had a 20 candle high breakout that looks fine on NQ, so I ran the exact same rules on ES and gold without changing a single number. Long only, stop and target off ATR, flat by the close. 15 minute candles, ten years, one contract, 100k account, commission and slippage charged on both sides.

|Market|Trades|Win rate|Profit factor|Net|Max drawdown|
|:-|:-|:-|:-|:-|:-|
|NQ|3,201|40.9%|1.09|**+91.75%**|16.3%|
|ES|3,093|38.8%|1.05|**+30.33%**|16.0%|
|GC|1,911|37.4%|0.90|**-48.19%**|53.2%|

**\_\_\_\_**

The win rates land within four points of each other across all three, so the rules are finding the same kind of move in every market. What changes is whether that move is big enough to pay for itself.

Before costs gold finished at **-0.42%**, basically flat across ten years. After commission and slippage it finished at **-48.19%**. The bill was $47,775 on 1,911 trades and that is the whole distance between a dead strategy and half the account gone. On NQ the same bill came to $32,010 across more trades, and NQ carried enough points per trade to cover it and still finish up 92%.

A profit factor of 1.09 means youre making a dollar nine back for every dollar you lose. **Theres no room in that for a wider spread or a smaller point value.** Which market you picked ends up doing more of the work than the entry rules do.

**\_\_\_\_**

Its a bit like pouring the same foundation on three different lots. Same blueprint and same crew, and on two of them the concrete sets fine. On the third the ground wont hold it.

One set of rules across three markets doesnt prove anything general, and there are limits on this one worth naming. This one is long only and gold spent a good chunk of the decade going sideways, which punishes a long breakout much harder than it punishes NQ. A short side would move the gold number and I havent run it yet. I also havent tried re-fitting the ATR multiples per market, which is the obvious next step and also the thing that quietly turns one test into three curve fits.

All three ran in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) off the same saved version so nothing differed except the symbol. Gold broke even before costs and lost half the account after them.
